IFP Portal / IFP Option Sketcher Utility

IFP Option Sketcher

Rapid shortlisting of RNAV approach and SID options against PANS-OPS nominal-track criteria. Not for operational use; feasible options go to full construction and obstacle assessment.

Criteria apply to every option in this project. Defaults follow Doc 8168 Vol II; check them against the edition and any UK variations you work to.

    Starts from a T-bar approach or a straight-out SID that you then reshape.

    Import coding table

    Excel coding tables (one or more per sheet) or a text-based AIP PDF. Each procedure found becomes a new option.

          How it works
          • Editing. Drag waypoints to move them. Hold Shift while dragging to snap to an AIP fix. Use Add WP mode and click the chart to add a waypoint after the selected one. Click the small + on a leg to insert a waypoint there. Delete removes the selected waypoint and Ctrl+Z undoes.
          • Climb, then turn. From the MAPt (or the DER, set in Setup) the aircraft climbs on track at the missed approach gradient (or PDG) until it reaches the turn altitude, then turns direct to the next waypoint. The turn point depends on where the climb starts: the lowest start altitude gives the latest turn point and the highest gives the earliest. Both are drawn and checked.
          • Colours. With "Colour track by compliance" on, the nominal track is green where no limits are exceeded, amber where a check needs attention and red where a limit is exceeded. Each finding colours the part of the track it applies to: the leg into a waypoint, the leg out of it or the turn itself. The dashed earliest-turn track is coloured by its own findings. Achieved profile altitudes appear under each waypoint's constraint: green when the constraint is met, red when it is not.
          • CAS containment. The nominal track, at its profile altitude, must be inside a CTR, CTA or TMA of Class A–E (or upper FIR/FRA airspace). Stretches that are not are shaded red and listed with the reason: outside the lateral limits, or below the base of the CTA overhead. ATZs and TMZs do not count. Optional vertical and lateral buffers are on the Criteria tab. Flight-level limits are compared directly with altitudes, so allow for QNH near FL boundaries.
          • Importing coding tables. Import reads Excel coding tables and text-based AIP PDFs. Fixes (IF, TF, DF, CF, RF) become waypoints using the table coordinates, or the AIP position when none is given. Remarks set the IAF, IF, FAF and MAPt. A CA after the MAPt becomes the climb-then-turn. The turn after the climb uses the direction on the CA row, or the next row's if the CA row has none; a conflict between the two is listed as a note. A CA with no fix after it, or an FM leg, ends at a placeholder waypoint placed where the climb reaches its altitude (or 5 NM for FM). Holds mark the MAHF and are not drawn. Speed limits in the table cap the segment speed. Anything approximated or skipped is listed under Findings as an Import note.
          • Legs. TF legs with fly-by or fly-over waypoints, and RF legs. A fly-over turn is followed by a direct-to the next waypoint. An RF leg is the arc tangent to the incoming track that passes through the next waypoint; its radius is checked against the bank limit at the segment speed.
          • Turns. TAS comes from the segment IAS at the higher of the altitudes at the start and end of the turn, with the option's ISA deviation. Rate of turn is capped at 3°/s. Speed and bank for a turn come from the segment that follows the waypoint.
          • Approach profile. Constrained altitudes before the MAPt are planned altitudes and are interpolated along track. The final gradient runs from the FAF to the threshold crossing height. The missed approach climbs from the MAPt at the missed approach gradient, and at-or-above constraints are checked against it.
          • SID profile. The climb starts at the DER at the screen height and follows the PDG. At-or-above constraints are checked, at-or-below constraints level the climb off, and no turn may start below the minimum turn height.
          • Simplifications. Still air, no protection areas and no obstacle assessment. Minimum stabilisation distance is approximated by turn anticipation plus a roll allowance. Runway thresholds come from the AIP; where only a displaced threshold is published, the DER may need moving in Setup.
